reference_sql:
SELECT CAST(timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts)) AS DATE) AS order_day,
       channel,
       COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE CAST(timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts)) AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-24' AND DATE '2025-12-26'
GROUP BY 1, 2
alternatives: SELECT CAST(date_trunc('day', timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts))) AS DATE) AS order_day, channel, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts)) >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-24 00:00:00' AND timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts)) < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-27 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1, 2

SELECT CAST(timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts)) AS DATE) AS order_day, channel, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-23 23:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-26 23:00:00' GROUP BY 1, 2

other_way.sql: SELECT CAST(timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts)) AS DATE) AS order_day, channel, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-23 23:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-26 23:00:00' GROUP BY 1, 2
other_way.tradeoff: Filtering order_ts on UTC bounds keeps the column bare, but you must work out the 1 hour winter offset yourself.

solver.query:
SELECT CAST((order_ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Amsterdam' AS DATE) AS order_day, channel, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE CAST((order_ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Amsterdam' AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-24' AND DATE '2025-12-26'
GROUP BY 1, 2
